title: SRE: Define breaker thresholds, hysteresis, and safe default configs per region/model class
creator: Rafael Mendes
body:
## Context
We need sane, safe-by-default breaker configs that prevent queue blowups / GPU pool saturation cascades during traffic spikes, while avoiding breaker flapping and minimizing customer-visible disruption. This ticket defines:
- baseline thresholds (open/close) for routing-level breakers per (region, model_class, tier)
- hysteresis + cooldown parameters (to prevent flapping)
- “safe default” config presets shipped with overload protection, to be used unless explicitly overridden

This work must align with:
- ADR-0148 (breaker state model + hysteresis)
- overload error taxonomy + HTTP mapping (ADR-0147)
- runtime bounded queues + shed points (ENG-4826/4827)
- observability + SLO accounting for overload-protected errors (ENG-4829/4830)

## Definitions
**Breaker scope (routing layer):** per (model, region, tier) with optional aggregation per model_class for defaulting.
**Model classes (initial):**
1) chat-small (<= ~8B, short context typical)
2) chat-medium (~10–30B)
3) chat-large (>= ~34B or high-cost per token)
4) long-context (any model w/ >16k enabled; treat separately due to prefill cost)
5) embeddings (non-streaming; high QPS, low per-request cost)

**Tiers (Hosted):** free, pro, enterprise. (Dedicated alignment tracked elsewhere; see ENG-4837)

**Primary overload signals (routing inputs):**
- runtime_queue_depth_p95 (per pool) and queue_wait_ms_p95
- gpu_pool_saturation (composite: SM util + active sequences + scheduler backlog)
- memory_pressure (KV-cache pressure / eviction rate; from runtime)
- error mix shift (rate of runtime shed reasons / 503s) as a secondary confirmation

## Goals / non-goals
**Goals**
- Open early enough to stop tail latency collapse (avoid “slow death” where everything times out)
- Prefer deterministic overload-protected responses (429/503 + Retry-After) over timeouts
- Avoid flapping (open/close oscillation) and avoid retry storms (stable Retry-After)
- Defaults must be conservative and safe across regions; tunable by SRE with guardrails

**Non-goals**
- Perfect per-model tuning. We’ll start with class presets and iterate using canary + post-launch review.

## Proposed hysteresis + state machine parameters (baseline)
Applies to all model classes unless overridden.

- **Sampling window:** 10s rolling window for signals; breaker evaluation every 2s.
- **Open condition must hold for:** 8s continuous (prevents transient spikes from opening).
- **Open -> Half-open transition (cooldown):** 45s.
- **Half-open trial:** allow 1% of normal admitted traffic (min 5 req/min) for 30s.
- **Half-open -> Closed:** if open-signals are below close thresholds for 30s.
- **Half-open -> Open:** if open-signals breach open thresholds for 6s.
- **Close hysteresis:** close thresholds are 15–25% lower than open thresholds (signal-dependent; details below).

Rationale: cooldown roughly matches observed recovery time for GPU pool queues to drain after a burst (us-east canary data: 25–60s depending on model class; see updates below). Half-open duration + small trial rate reduces the chance we immediately re-saturate.

## Default breaker thresholds (v1)
All thresholds are defined per (region, model_class, tier) but shipped as presets per region + class. Tiers adjust the *admission weights* and *Retry-After* but thresholds should not be drastically different by tier (fairness + predictability). Where tier differences are required, we apply small deltas.

### Shared open/close signals
We evaluate the breaker open condition when any of the following are true (OR), with the “hold for N seconds” requirement.

1) **Queue depth** (strongest indicator)
- Open if runtime_queue_depth_p95 >= Q_OPEN for 8s
- Close if runtime_queue_depth_p95 <= Q_CLOSE for 30s

2) **Queue wait time** (captures latency spiral even if depth isn’t enormous)
- Open if queue_wait_ms_p95 >= W_OPEN for 8s
- Close if queue_wait_ms_p95 <= W_CLOSE for 30s

3) **GPU saturation composite** (backstop)
- Open if gpu_pool_saturation >= S_OPEN for 10s AND (queue_depth OR queue_wait) is trending up
- Close if gpu_pool_saturation <= S_CLOSE for 30s

4) **Memory/KV-cache pressure** (protect against OOM / thrash)
- Open if kv_evictions_per_s >= E_OPEN for 10s OR kv_cache_pressure >= P_OPEN for 8s
- Close if kv_cache_pressure <= P_CLOSE for 60s

### Preset values by model class (baseline, us-east/us-west/eu-central)
Note: queue depth here is “requests pending in runtime queue per pool shard” as exported by runtime. We intentionally keep these low to prefer shedding over long queues.

**chat-small**
- Q_OPEN: 120, Q_CLOSE: 90
- W_OPEN: 900ms, W_CLOSE: 600ms
- S_OPEN: 0.92, S_CLOSE: 0.82
- Memory pressure: P_OPEN 0.85, P_CLOSE 0.75 (normalized)
- Retry-After default: 1s (pro/enterprise), 2s (free)

**chat-medium**
- Q_OPEN: 90, Q_CLOSE: 65
- W_OPEN: 1100ms, W_CLOSE: 750ms
- S_OPEN: 0.90, S_CLOSE: 0.80
- Memory pressure: P_OPEN 0.83, P_CLOSE 0.72
- Retry-After default: 2s (pro/enterprise), 3s (free)

**chat-large**
- Q_OPEN: 55, Q_CLOSE: 40
- W_OPEN: 1400ms, W_CLOSE: 950ms
- S_OPEN: 0.88, S_CLOSE: 0.78
- Memory pressure: P_OPEN 0.80, P_CLOSE 0.70
- Retry-After default: 3s (pro/enterprise), 5s (free)

**long-context**
- Q_OPEN: 35, Q_CLOSE: 25
- W_OPEN: 1800ms, W_CLOSE: 1200ms
- S_OPEN: 0.86, S_CLOSE: 0.76
- Memory pressure: P_OPEN 0.78, P_CLOSE 0.68
- Retry-After default: 5s (pro/enterprise), 8s (free)

**embeddings**
- Q_OPEN: 200, Q_CLOSE: 150
- W_OPEN: 600ms, W_CLOSE: 350ms
- S_OPEN: 0.93, S_CLOSE: 0.85
- Memory pressure: P_OPEN 0.88, P_CLOSE 0.80
- Retry-After default: 1s (all tiers)

### APAC / smaller regions preset adjustments
For smaller regions with less headroom (e.g., ap-southeast), use stricter queue-based thresholds:
- Multiply Q_OPEN and Q_CLOSE by 0.85
- Multiply W_OPEN and W_CLOSE by 0.90
- Increase cooldown from 45s -> 60s (slower drain / higher sensitivity to bursts)

## Tier behavior notes (Hosted)
- Thresholds are shared by tier (by default). We rely on admission control weights (gateway) and per-tier quotas to prioritize enterprise under contention.
- Retry-After differs by tier (above), but must remain stable per breaker-open epoch to avoid clients “probing” too aggressively.
- When breaker is OPEN, gateway should prefer returning the standardized overload-protected error with Retry-After; routing may still allow a trickle for enterprise if configured (policy guardrails via ENG-4838).

## Safe defaults + guardrails
We will ship a “safe default” config that is:
- enabled behind feature flags per region/model (rollout ticket ENG-4834)
- bounded in allowed ranges (config validation):
  - cooldown: 15s–180s
  - half-open trial %: 0.5%–5%
  - Q_OPEN minimums: chat-small>=60, chat-large>=25 (avoid opening on very small blips)
  - Q_OPEN maximums: chat-small<=250, chat-large<=100 (avoid unbounded queues)
- changes require SRE approval (oncall policy) once globally enabled

## Acceptance criteria
- [x] Document v1 thresholds + hysteresis parameters per region/model class
- [x] Provide initial presets file (schema draft in Drive) values + rationale
- [x] Review with Routing (Mina/Ravi) + Runtime (Noah/Lena) + Observability (Allison)
- [x] Canary plan includes explicit “tuning knobs” and rollback thresholds
- [x] Explicit note on how these interact with Retry-After values and avoiding retry storms

## Links / references
- Working notes (thresholds + hysteresis): Google Drive: overload-thresholds-and-hysteresis-working-notes
- Policy matrix (layer->HTTP mapping): Drive: load-shedding-policy-matrix-sheet
- ADR-0148: circuit breaker state model and hysteresis
- Dashboard + alerting: ENG-4830

## Open questions (tracked as follow-ups)
1) Should W_OPEN differ for streaming vs non-streaming endpoints? (runtime says queue_wait captures both but streaming decode behavior may warrant separate signal)
2) For long-context, should we incorporate “prefill_concurrency” as first-class open signal? (runtime to advise)
3) Whether embeddings should use separate “tokenization time” vs queue_wait to avoid false opens.

Follow-up tickets:
- ENG-4840 (alert tuning post-canary)
- ENG-4831 (perf test scenarios that validate these thresholds)
comments: 2025-10-22 (Christine Wong): Drafted initial class-based presets (chat-small/medium/large/long-context/embeddings). Biggest question is whether we bias toward queue_depth vs queue_wait. I’m leaning queue_depth primary because it’s less endpoint-dependent. Syncing with Runtime on what “queue depth” means post ENG-4826.

2025-10-24 (Lena Fischer): Runtime queue depth metric is per scheduler shard; p95 is a good aggregator. Please avoid absolute thresholds that assume shard count; ideally thresholds should be normalized or derived from max_concurrency. If we can’t do that in v1, at least note shard-count dependency in docs.

2025-10-28 (Ravi Menon): Routing can support per-(model,region,tier) overrides but we need tight guardrails to avoid per-customer snowflakes. Agree with class presets + small region adjustment factor. Also: we should keep tier differences mostly in admission weights, not breaker thresholds.

2025-11-02 (Allison Grant): For observability, please ensure every breaker transition emits (reason, signal snapshot). Also avoid high-cardinality labels like raw model version; use model_family/model_class for defaults. If you need model-specific overrides, keep them in config, not metric labels.

2025-11-10 (Rafael Mendes): Adding note: Retry-After must be stable while OPEN to reduce clients hammering. Prefer stepwise values (1/2/3/5/8s) vs dynamic jitter from server; client should add jitter.

2025-12-04 (Tomáš Novák): From incident review, the biggest pain is tail-latency collapse before we see a clear saturation signal. Suggest W_OPEN be relatively aggressive, especially for long-context, to avoid 60–120s timeouts. Also please set cooldown long enough to actually drain.

2025-12-18 (Christine Wong): Updated presets after us-east dry run in staging: long-context Q_OPEN reduced (45 -> 35) and cooldown increased (30s -> 45s). Observed recovery time ~40–70s after burst; 45s seems safer for preventing immediate re-open.

2026-01-07 (Sean Gallagher): Exec update asked specifically whether these defaults are ‘safe globally’. Answer: yes as a starting point; we’ll tune per smaller regions (ap-southeast) with stricter thresholds and longer cooldown. Please make sure that’s called out clearly in the doc so we don’t surprise Support.
2026-01-09 (Christine Wong): Marking Done for v1: thresholds written up + shared with Routing/Runtime/Obs. Post-canary tuning will be tracked under ENG-4840 once we have 7–10 days of data.
